A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Moral Alignment for LLM Agents, with matching methods and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison, including identification of relocated content and a removed appendix analysis.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM fine-tuning, learning and unlearning experiments, cross-game evaluations, robustness analyses and qualitative follow-up responses.

after.justification: v4 retains original fine-tuning, learning and unlearning results, cross-game and cross-prompt evaluations, and appendix robustness and baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: Both versions use Gemma2-2b-it, PPO with LoRA, the same intrinsic reward functions and the same sequential fine-tuning variants. Clarifying that the state contains both players' previous actions agrees with v3's existing state equation and training prompt.

E1.justification: v4 removes the post-decision explanation task in v3 Appendix 8.12, where models answered questions about their reasons and strategies. The five matrix games, four IPD prompt variants and three generic action prompts remain; the explicit IPD evaluation is reorganized rather than removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding retained comparisons use the same untuned, Game-reward and morally fine-tuned models. Both value-prompted baselines remain in v3 Figure 25 and v4 Figure 26. Corrections to their displayed prompts do not introduce different comparison methods.

E3.justification: Appendix 8.8 changes its stated evaluation tokens from action1/action2 to action3/action4, and several prompt examples correct mixed token names. These revise documented evaluation inputs, but v3 already labels the corresponding results with the new tokens, so reruns are not established. Training budgets, metrics and evaluation lengths remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 removes the qualitative case study asking whether models can justify their decisions, including v3 Appendix 8.12 and Figures 26–27. Token-reversal, payoff-permutation, prompt-format, opponent and reciprocity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages across five seeds/runs and the same 95% confidence-interval practice. Appendix 8.1 retains the exclusion of early runs that never produced legal tokens. No statistical procedure or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The retained quantitative plots have identical underlying graphics, with unchanged learning, moral-regret and action-choice results. v4 removes the sample responses in v3 Figure 27 and the finding that none of the sampled morally fine-tuned models invoked prosociality or moral policies when explaining their decisions.

T1.justification: The reward functions, state representation and moral-regret definition retain their mathematical meaning. Replacing square brackets with braces around legal actions in Table 1 is a notation correction. No theorem, proof or substantive derivation is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims about alignment through explicit intrinsic rewards, unlearning selfish behavior and transferring some moral strategies across games. Added emphasis on transparency and customized or pluralistic alignment reiterates ideas already present in v3.

C2.justification: Appendix 8.7 adds an attribution of noisier LLM-opponent results to multi-agent learning. Appendix 8.8 refines the interpretation of action choices toward possible token-order matching. The discussion of game-theoretic versus explicitly moral justifications in v3 Appendix 8.12 is removed.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly specifies training on a single A100 or V100 GPU with up to 40GB VRAM. The code footnote changes from a promise of release upon acceptance to a concrete repository link. Existing hyperparameters and software versions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds supporting citations to Berglund et al. on situational awareness, Sharma et al. on sycophancy, Schick et al. on Toolformer and Yan et al. on LLM priors for RL. The main research positioning remains unchanged; other title and publication updates concern existing cited works.

P1.justification: v4 locally rewrites explanations, particularly Sections 2.1 and 8.8, corrects wording and cross-references, and adds acknowledgments and updated author/publication information. The main section sequence and argument remain intact, with the localized removal of Appendix 8.12.

P2.justification: Prompt figures are extensively redesigned with shaded boxes and monospaced text, and the existing training prompt is also reproduced as main-text Figure 2. Appendix figures and Table 3 are substantially regrouped and relocated, while former Figures 26–27 are removed. Retained quantitative graphics preserve their content.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility and readability through corrected evaluation-token documentation, hardware disclosure, a concrete code link and clearer prompt displays. Removing Appendix 8.12 sacrifices useful qualitative evidence about models' lack of explicitly moral justifications, but this was a small illustrative analysis. The quantitative evidence and central generalization caveats remain, supporting a limited net improvement.
